components.name: Analysis 1: Analysis on the Real Line
Education and Communication
components.note: Study theories of learning and mathematical communication, then develop a group teaching or communication project with a report and presentation.

components.name: Combinatorial enumeration
components.note: Selected six-credit mathematics option in year two. Combinatorial counting uses generating functions, recurrence equations and formal power series; earlier groups, rings and fields provide the recommended background.

components.name: Complex Analysis
components.note: Selected six-credit mathematics option in year two. Complex differentiation, contour integration, residues and Taylor and Laurent series build on the earlier analysis courses.

components.name: Approved Free Electives
components.note: Six genuinely free credits in year two and twenty-four in year three remain open. Selection needs Examination Board approval for overlap and level; programme mathematics options are approved. Normally at most twelve free credits may be introductory. UvA and VU minors have the stated introductory-level exception.

components.name: Reflection on Mathematics
components.note: Examine ethical and societal questions in mathematics, including financial models, cryptography, privacy, algorithms and AI.

components.name: Bachelor Project in Mathematics
components.note: Entry requires at least 132 credits from the Mathematics programme. The example completes 120 credits in years one and two and eighteen restricted mathematics credits in the first two periods of year three before the January project start. Individually supervised research produces a thesis, presentation and oral defence.

components.name: Introduction to Information Theory
components.note: Selected six-credit mathematics option in the first semester of year three. Study probability-based entropy, compression, coding and security, including proofs.

components.name: Differential Geometry (BSc)
components.note: Selected six-credit mathematics option in the first semester of year three. Smooth manifolds, differential forms and integration build on analysis, linear algebra and topology.

components.name: Functional Analysis (BSc)
components.note: Selected six-credit mathematics option in the first semester of year three. Study infinite-dimensional linear spaces and mappings, building on compulsory analysis and linear algebra.

components.name: Approved Free Electives
components.note: Twenty-four free credits remain open. A thirty-credit minor or approved foreign semester has separate redistribution rules, including a mathematics choice in year two and a conditional replacement of Reflection on Mathematics. This example retains the ordinary route and Reflection course.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three evidence-backed programmes retained after current content and full schedule repair. The strongest response combines mathematical methods, proof and computational/applied modelling; data-oriented inference and economic optimisation change the academic priorities and actual courses. Pairwise differences are5,8and7courses, not arbitrary substitutions. Pure mathematics depth remains a material gap, but the mathematical core, algorithms and applications provide genuine programme-level comparability. Computer-science and physics stable directions remain explicit maximum-reached candidates; no formal double degree or fourth alternative is claimed.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both explicitly teach sets, functions/relations, proof strategies and induction. UvA additionally develops number systems, cardinality and divisibility; this is partial correspondence.
Both study graphs and algorithms on networks. UCR emphasizes traversal, paths, trees and algorithmic complexity; UvA also develops graph-theoretic properties and colouring.
Both introduce Python programming for problem-solving. UvA applies it to mathematical experiments; UCR also develops recursion and object-oriented software.
Both develop single-variable differentiation and integration. UvA combines calculations with proof-oriented real analysis; UCR also uses computer algebra and dynamic models.
Both study vector spaces, linear maps, eigenvalues and orthogonality; UCR adds computational and statistical applications.
Both study computer-based solution of equations and numerical error. UCR offers a broader numerical-methods programme; UvA’s introduction includes SVD and sensitivity to small errors.
Both extend calculus to several variables. UCR’s description also supports differential equations and complex-valued functions, but not the complete proof/theorem structure of UvA analysis.

Both treat differential equations and stability. UCR concentrates on linear systems, signals and transforms; UvA additionally develops existence/uniqueness, nonlinear planar dynamics and periodic behaviour.
Both study probability spaces, conditional probability, random variables and distributions. UCR also includes inference and Monte Carlo methods.
Both examine ethical and societal questions around algorithms, AI, privacy and responsibility. UvA explicitly frames these questions through the profession and wider uses of mathematics.

Both implement mathematical models of population change using software. UCR’s ecological modelling is a smaller part of a broad ecology course; UvA centres disease ODE models, interventions and parameter estimation.
Both address estimation, tests and statistical inference. UCR develops applied multivariable models and diagnostics; UvA examines statistical procedures in a mathematical framework.

notes.text: UvA provides a sustained proof-oriented sequence in analysis, abstract algebra, geometry and topology, followed by named advanced mathematics choices and a compulsory bachelor project. UCR offers meaningful calculus, linear algebra, proof and discrete reasoning, probability, numerical methods and linear systems with substantial computational applications. It does not reproduce that full pure-mathematics sequence. UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 credits.

audience.programmeDescription: The University of Amsterdam’s Mathematics bachelor builds a common foundation in proof, analysis, algebra, probability and mathematical skills, followed by advanced mathematics choices, free electives and an individual research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programmes develop mathematical and computational methods through modelling, data analysis or economic optimisation. UvA offers a more extensive pure-mathematics sequence, including abstract algebra, geometry, topology and advanced analysis. UCR’s proof and applied mathematical work provides real overlap while those differences remain substantial.

cellNotes.text: Both explicitly teach sets, functions/relations, proof strategies and induction. UvA additionally develops number systems, cardinality and divisibility; this is partial correspondence.
Both study graphs and algorithms on networks. UCR emphasizes traversal, paths, trees and algorithmic complexity; UvA also develops graph-theoretic properties and colouring.
Both introduce Python programming for problem-solving. UvA applies it to mathematical experiments; UCR also develops recursion and object-oriented software.
Both develop single-variable differentiation and integration. UvA combines calculations with proof-oriented real analysis; UCR also uses computer algebra and dynamic models.
Both study vector spaces, linear maps, eigenvalues and orthogonality; UCR adds computational and statistical applications.
Both study computer-based solution of equations and numerical error. UCR offers a broader numerical-methods programme; UvA’s introduction includes SVD and sensitivity to small errors.
Both extend calculus to several variables. UCR’s description also supports differential equations and complex-valued functions, but not the complete proof/theorem structure of UvA analysis.

Both treat differential equations and stability. UCR concentrates on linear systems, signals and transforms; UvA additionally develops existence/uniqueness, nonlinear planar dynamics and periodic behaviour.
Both study probability spaces, conditional probability, random variables and distributions. UCR also includes inference and Monte Carlo methods.
Both examine ethical and societal questions around algorithms, AI, privacy and responsibility. UvA explicitly frames these questions through the profession and wider uses of mathematics.

Both implement mathematical models of population change using software. UCR’s ecological modelling is a smaller part of a broad ecology course; UvA centres disease ODE models, interventions and parameter estimation.
Both address estimation, tests and statistical inference. UCR develops applied multivariable models and diagnostics; UvA examines statistical procedures in a mathematical framework.
Group theory has no dedicated UCR counterpart; algebraic algorithms do not reproduce the study of groups and their structure.
Rings, ideals, field extensions and finite fields have no dedicated UCR counterpart.
The dedicated vector-field, surface-integral and Stokes-theorem course has no sufficiently documented separate UCR counterpart.
The course addresses theories of learning mathematics and mathematical communication; generic project reporting does not reproduce that educational function.
Topological spaces, compactness, homotopy and fundamental groups are not supplied by UCR’s applied modelling courses.
This is the twelve-credit Mathematics bachelor research project. UCR’s optional independent research is shown separately from its scheduled 180 credits.
